newsitem.title: USA: Dlr/mark ends at new high in U.S., stg/mark leads.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark ends at new high in U.S., stg/mark leads.

text.p: The dollar ended higher after posting a new three-and-a-half-year high against the mark on the back of rising German joblessness and another jump in sterling/mark, dealers said.

The most powerful move of the day came as the pound soared in the wake of data showing the annual rate of British retail price inflation pushed up to 2.9 percent in June, exceeding expectations and heightening fears of an interest rates hike.
"On the back of sterling/mark, dollar/mark broke through 1.76," said Gabriel Grippo, senior trader at Credit Agricole Indosuez.
The dollar surpassed 1.76 marks for the first time since Feburary 1994, aided by broad mark weakness after Germany reported an 11,000 rise in unemployment for June.

The dollar ended at 1.7617/27 marks -- its high of the day -- compared with 1.7540/50 at the open. Dollar/yen rose late in the afternoon to 113.12/22 yen, from 112.60/70 after spending most of the session orbiting opening levels.

Germany has been contending with the worst job market of the post-World War II period this year and odds of any mark-supporting interest rate hike dim on every report showing the economy shedding jobs, analysts said.

The juxtaposition of Germany's struggling economy against overheated U.K. growth encouraged traders to dump marks for sterling, which pushed the pound to 2.9758, its highest level against the mark since May 1991, said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank in Chicago.
"The German unemployment number just continues to underline some of the domestic problems they're having and you also have talk of a base rate hike by the end of the week in the U.K.," Nelson said.
Mark/yen dipped to a 23-month low of 63.99, curbing the dollar's advance against the buoyant Japanese currency.

The yen continues to derive strength from a recently swelling Japanese trade surplus, and trading was cautious ahead of the release of May data on the surplus in Japan's current account, due at 2350 GMT on Tuesday.
Booming Japanese exports have set off alarms in Washington and complaints that dollar/yen's rise earlier this year has flooded the U.S. with underpriced Japanese products.

"The trade figures have already been released, but on a different basis -- customs cleared. They were up 222 percent, year over year," said David Gilmore, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics, a Connecticut consulting firm.
"We should expect between a 100- and 200-percent year-over-year increase in the current account surlus as a result," Gilmore added.
In other trade, the dollar rose to 1.4650/60 Swiss francs from 1.4630/40 at the open. It fell to Canadian $1.3736/41 from C$1.3770/75.
The dollar ended a bit higher against the pound, which eased to $1.6865/75 from $1.6925/35. The Australian dollar rose to $0.7465/70 from $0.7435/40.
